name: doc-card
purpose: One cell of the grid a documentation page scans across: a leading glyph, an optional eyebrow, the title, the copy, and an optional call-to-action row at the foot. It renders as an anchor when it has an `href` and as a plain block when it does not, so a card is either a destination or a statement — never a dead link.
useWhen: A grid of peer destinations: "what you can build", the product tiles a landing section opens with.
A set of short, scannable entries whose titles carry most of the meaning.
avoidWhen: When each entry needs a sentence to be understood — use `DocItem` rows, one column, so every description is read at the page's own measure instead of squeezed into a cell.
For a single call to action at the end of a page — that is a button, not a card.
For an application surface — use `Card`, which is the console's carded surface.
related: DocCardGroup` — the frame and grid this is a cell of; a card outside one has no cell ring.
DocItem` — the row counterpart. A card claims a whole tile; a row claims one line.
bestPractices: Keep the title to a noun phrase and let the copy carry the verb.
Use `eyebrow` only when the title alone does not say who or when; it is not a category label.
Set `link-label` when the card should close on an explicit call to action; otherwise the whole tile being the link is enough.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small muted line above the title — who makes the thing, when the title does not say.

props.name: icon
props.doc: PrimeIcons class for the leading glyph. Ignored when the `icon` slot is filled.

props.name: href
props.doc: Destination; when set the whole card becomes the link.

props.name: label
props.doc: Fallback copy when the default slot is empty.

props.name: linkLabel
props.doc: Call-to-action text; when set the card closes on a link row.

slots.name: icon
slots.notes: The leading mark, when a font glyph will not do. Replaces `icon`.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import DocCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card'
</script>

<template>
  <DocCard
    title="Edge Application"
    icon="pi pi-server"
    href="/docs/edge-application"
    link-label="Read the guide"
  >
    Serve and cache your application at the edge, close to the people using it.
  </DocCard>
</template>
